conventions.convention: X is finite and nonempty, k ≥ 1, all reference weights are strictly positive, and canonical parameters range over all of R^k. Minimality excludes every nonzero direction making the statistic constant.
Relative interior means interior in the affine hull with its Euclidean subspace topology.
The MLE theorem uses an IID product sampling model with n ≥ 1; a finite MLE must attain the likelihood maximum at a parameter in R^k.
The supporting direction is a Euclidean unit vector u satisfying u·(T(x)−μ) ≤ 0. The boundary-MLE proof therefore increases the likelihood along positive u.

The latent model has a proper probability prior, a measurable canonical-parameter map, and a parameter-and-configuration measurable observation kernel. Dominated models additionally specify a sigma-finite data measure and a jointly measurable normalized density.

Posterior-kernel existence assumes AC and standard-Borel parameter and data spaces. Posterior uniqueness is only data-marginal almost everywhere; the density ratio is used where its predictive normalizer is finite and strictly positive.

Pseudo-likelihood multiplies exact one-site conditional probabilities using the same fixed exterior boundary and finite interaction collection. It is an objective, not a normalized configuration probability law.

load_bearing.statement: For finite nonempty X, k ≥ 1, positive w and T:X→R^k, define Z(θ)=Σx w(x)exp(θ·T(x)), A(θ)=log Z(θ), and πθ(x)=w(x)exp(θ·T(x)−A(θ)). The representation is minimal when no nonzero a makes a·T constant on X.

The following conditions are equivalent: the representation is minimal; no nonzero a makes a·T(x) constant on X; the affine hull of T(X) is R^k; the Hessian of A is positive definite at every parameter; and θ↦πθ is injective.
A proper prior Π and an observation probability kernel K give the marginal sampling kernel Q(θ,B)=Σx πϑ(θ)(x)K((θ,x),B). In the dominated case its density is L(θ,y)=Σx πϑ(θ)(x)k(y|θ,x).
For a finite nonempty X and T:X→R^k with full affine hull, if μ belongs to K=conv(T(X)) but is not interior to K, there is a Euclidean unit vector u such that u·(T(x)−μ) ≤ 0 for every x∈X.

For a minimal finite exponential family and a realized IID tuple of length n ≥ 1, a finite MLE exists if and only if the empirical statistic mean belongs to the relative interior of conv(T(X)); when it exists it is unique.
For the specified finite-volume Gibbs law with fixed boundary, PLθ(σ) is the product over sites of the exact conditional probability of the observed site spin given all other spins.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite-family normalization, C² log-partition regularity, gradient-as-mean and Hessian-as-covariance; the finite counting-measure model verifies its compact-parameter envelope hypothesis.
Coordinate inner products, norm formulas, supporting directions and quadratic forms.
Compact-parameter exponential envelopes, nearest points in the polytope, and attainment of the coercive likelihood objective on a closed ball.
Continuity bounds, norm properties and convergence of supporting inequalities.
Definition and finite real values of the exponential and the constant e.
Logarithm domain and inverse identities in normalization and log likelihoods.
Positive Gibbs masses, nonzero denominators and reciprocal exponential identities.
Exponential envelope bounds, continuity and Borel measurability, and the strict inequality e > 1.
A proper span of statistic differences has a nonzero orthogonal direction.
Product and quotient log likelihoods and equivalence of likelihood and log-likelihood maximization.

Identifiability proof: constant statistic directions multiply the partition function by exp(tc). Also identifies the missing explicit supplier for common-energy cancellation in the pseudo-likelihood proof.
Compactness of the finite coefficient simplex without a choice assumption.
Compactness of the finite convex hull as a simplex image.
Closedness of the finite convex hull.
Closed inverse images in the coefficient-simplex compactness argument; only choice-free implications are used.
A fixed enumeration of rational vectors for canonical exterior approximants.
Countability of the finite Cartesian power of the rationals.
A surjective rational-vector enumeration and least-index selection without countable choice.
Coordinatewise rational approximation of points outside the closed polytope.
A convergent subsequence of unit supporting directions; the supplier explicitly states a choice-free proof.
Compactness of the positive-radius ball used to attain the MLE objective.
Strict concavity from a negative second derivative and strict monotonicity of the all-plus log likelihood.
The proper-prior and parameter-measurable probability-kernel interface.
Product measurability and measurable fixed-configuration sections of the observation kernel.
Pointwise probability measures and measurable evaluations for sampling and posterior kernels.
The explicit choice hypothesis inherited from the general posterior-kernel existence theorem.
The measurable-space hypotheses of posterior existence and simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness.
Posterior-kernel existence, rectangle identities and uniqueness outside one data-marginal null set under AC.
Measurability of predictive densities and posterior numerators, exchange of nonnegative integrals, and verification of the dominated posterior formula.
Differentiation of the all-plus Bernoulli-spin likelihood.
The logarithm derivative in the all-plus likelihood calculation.
Scalar exponential and logarithm compositions in the all-plus example.
Sum and scalar-multiple derivative rules in the all-plus example.

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.1 says potentials indexed by sets not containing i are common to all candidate spins and 'cancel', establishing dependence only on N_i. Factoring that common additive energy out of the exponential requires exp(a+b)=exp(a)exp(b), but the declared suppliers provide only the exponential definition, positivity/reciprocity, and continuity/monotonicity. The neighborhood claim is correct; its proof should explicitly identify the exponential addition law, for example the already available thm-exponential-addition-formula.
